title: Tenant search with generation-keyed result cache
name: Tenant search service

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code makes sure searches do not return results from before a document update? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Why does the cache key contain a per-tenant generation number rather than the code deleting cached entries when a document is indexed?
choices: Deleting entries is not supported by TtlCache
The set of cached queries for a tenant is unknown, so bumping the generation makes all old entries unreachable at once
Generation numbers make cache lookups faster than string keys
It prevents other tenants from seeing each other's results

questions.prompt: After many writes to a tenant, entries stored under old generations are never read again. How do they leave memory?
choices: They are removed by get() the next time any search runs
They are removed when indexDocument bumps the generation
They are removed by the scheduled evictExpired task after their TTL passes
They are never removed, so the map grows without bound

questions.prompt: Tenant A's documents are updated constantly while tenant B's never change. What is the effect on tenant B's cached searches?
choices: They are invalidated every time tenant A bumps its generation
They stay valid until their own TTL, since B's generation never changes
They are invalidated only when tenant A's queries are identical
They expire immediately because the sweeper cannot tell tenants apart
